correctness.rationale: A direct event argument avoids assuming generator-domain regularity or a finite mean in advance. Set S=α+β. From the reset site while inactive, the time to go active has rate α+rηπ₁: all other reset outcomes leave the searcher at that same state. Its mean is Δ=S/[α(S+rη)]. Starting active, measure time only while active. A direct reset occurs at rate r; an off excursion begins at rate β, lasts an independent Exp(α+r), and ends in a position reset with probability r/(α+r). If it ends in reactivation, the active Markov motion continues from the same state. Thus in active time the first disruptive reset has rate q=r+βr/(α+r), is independent of the active path, and competes with τ. A cycle succeeds with probability F(q) and uses mean active time d=(1−F(q))/q. The expected wall-clock time including all off waits until reset or success is d[1+β/(α+r)]. After a direct reset the inactive probability is ηπ₀; after a reset during an off period it is 1−ηπ₁. Including the time to return to active at x_* adds d[rηπ₀+βr(1−ηπ₁)/(α+r)]Δ to the cycle cost. The combined multiplier of d is exactly S/α. By regeneration at active x_* and F(q)>0 the mean is finite and equals Sd/[αF(q)], independent of η. Stationary initialization adds π₀Δ, giving the formula and strict improvement for η'>η. This is a mean identity only, and geometry independence concerns the penalty at a common starting and reset site, not arbitrary initial sites or the full mean itself. The finite-state script and recorded comparisons were inspected, not executed.
residual_risks: The active-clock argument uses strict immobilization and no unmodeled memory during an off excursion, plus independent Poisson/exponential clocks. F(q)=0 is excluded.

value.rationale: This answers a natural protocol-design question: when does the mean benefit of forgetting an internal mode depend on the search geometry? It identifies all geometry dependence in one active first-passage transform and shows why the benefit at the reset point comes solely from stationary initialization into the frozen state. The exact penalty and active-start invariance apply without solving the spatial process, even when its original mean first-passage time is infinite.
residual_risks: No stochastic ordering, arbitrary non-reset initial location, or extension to a moving inactive state is established.
